open_points.subject: MCP product actions (K-11 versus Primary actions)
open_points.text: “The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.” This omits the separately specified actions “add a trial case”, “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus”, “release a failed run”, “roll a slot back”, “propose an operation binding”, and “compose and prove a flow”, and calls activation an owner's operation although an agent may request read-only activation.
open_points.question: Which primary actions are distinct MCP operations, which are variants of the listed operations, and may agents invoke activation for proven read-only versions through that surface?
options: Every Primary actions row is exposed as a distinct typed MCP operation with its stated actors
The omitted actions are subcommands of `author`, `inspect`, or `activate`
K-11 is exhaustive and the omitted primary actions are not externally callable
open_points.default_guess: Expose every Primary actions row as a typed MCP operation and allow agent-requested activation only for proven read-only versions.

open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” But its facts include “the TrialExecutions (M07) this admission ran”, and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time”; those executions have freshly minted identities and timestamps.
open_points.question: When an equal implementation is submitted again against the same corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict observation created with new TrialExecutions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not rerun admission
Rerun admission and create a new entity verdict
Rerun admission but replace or revise the existing value verdict
open_points.default_guess: Rerun admission and create a new entity verdict that references the new TrialExecutions.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” The carried decision also says “a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes)”, while an OperationBinding can change from `proposed` to `accepted`.
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can produce different results as binding state changes?
options: ProofResult is an observation entity for a particular proof attempt
ProofResult is a value derived from the flow version plus the relevant current binding states
Only the latest computed result exists and earlier results have no model identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a value derived from the flow version and the binding states used by that proof.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution
open_points.text: Its identity is declared “value”, but it is “the trace record of one concluded attempt”, is identified by `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index`, and `attempt_number`, and says “an attempt's record is issued once.” M07 states that an execution observation issued once is an entity rather than a value.
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution an occurrence entity identified by its run/node/element/attempt coordinates, or a substitutable content value?
options: Value whose identity is derived from all meaning facts
Value identified only by the attempt coordinates
open_points.default_guess: Make it an entity with the composite attempt coordinates as its identity.

open_points.subject: Function implementation inspection and K-12 repair context
open_points.text: State 0 permits owner and agent to “inspect functions”, M05 says code is “shown to the agent repairing its slot”, and K-12 says “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies.” No action or request fact distinguishes repair inspection from composition inspection.
open_points.question: Which product action lets an agent enter the repair view and read an implementation body, and what does ordinary function inspection return?
options: `inspect` has an explicit repair mode scoped to one slot
Any function inspection returns implementation bodies, while composition listing omits them
A separate repair action returns the one-slot repair bundle
open_points.default_guess: Give `inspect` an explicit one-slot repair form; ordinary composition-oriented inspection returns contracts and bindings without implementation bodies.

open_points.subject: M28 Installation
open_points.text: Installation is declared a value—“equal configuration is the same installation”—but “the token list is read again whenever it has changed”, so configuration facts can change while existing durable records continue to describe actors and the same running kernel.
open_points.question: Does a configuration change create a new Installation identity, or mutate/revise the configuration of the same installation, and which configuration fields besides tokens can change without restart?
options: Installation is an entity that retains identity while configured facts change
Each configuration snapshot is a new Installation value
Only agent tokens are live facts; all other changes require restart and create a new configuration snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Treat the deployed installation as a continuing entity, with agent-token configuration live-reloaded and all other listed configuration read only at startup.
